items.text: When deadline expires in join(), break skips terminate() for current and remaining processes, allowing flushers from old assignment to outlive rebalance; process_index is unused and remaining_time check duplicates inner while-loop's deadline check
The break at line 340 exits the entire for loop when the deadline expires, so terminate() is skipped for all remaining processes even if the isinstance bug were fixed
_create_process_for_shard (lines 127-132) has no callers and is dead code since restarts go through _create_process_for_shards.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
No test covers restart/kill path or flushing across multiple processes; test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internals without checking segments from all shards are flushed

On hang restart, the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard is always False for spawn-context processes (SpawnProcess), so kill() never runs. This allows old processes to keep running while replacements start on the same shards, causing duplicate segment reads and up to 10 orphaned processes per index holding Redis and Kafka connections.
process.kill() in _ensure_processes_alive is a regression since the pre-PR code called it unconditionally, meaning unhealthy/hung processes are now never killed before spawning a replacement
max_processes normalised twice, self.max_processes kept only for test, and _create_processes is 2-line wrapper with one caller

Remove the unused `_create_process_for_shard` method or document if it's reserved for future use. The method at lines 127-132 has no callers in the codebase and only delegates to `_create_process_for_shards`. If not intended for public API or future extension, it should be removed to reduce maintenance burden.

SpanFlusher.join(timeout=...) can break out of its per-process loop once the deadline expires, leaving remaining flusher processes running after join returns, which can leak background processes during shutdown/rebalancing
time.sleep(0.1) delay is a no-op because test_basic already monkeypatches time.sleep to lambda _: None, so it does not actually give the flusher thread time to run.
--flusher-processes is plain int with no lower bound; 0 silently means one process per shard; negative value gives num_processes < 0, empty process_to_shards_map and KeyError from i % n
Having both _create_process_for_shard and _create_process_for_shards methods with near-identical names is confusing for future maintainers

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
terminate() at line 346 uses same wrong isinstance(multiprocessing.Process) check that was already broken
submit() calls get_memory_info() and record_stored_segments() once per per-process buffer against same Redis cluster, causing N times the round trips on consumer's main thread for no new information

The spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce metric timer uses tag key 'shards' (plural) while all other metrics in the same function use 'shard' (singular), causing inconsistent metric grouping and breaking dashboard consistency
Metric tag key inconsistent: 'shards' at line 199 but 'shard' at lines 185, 195, 244; value sometimes comma-joined shard list, sometimes int; joined lists change on rebalance raising tag cardinality

In join(), terminate() is behind the same wrong isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check, so it never runs for SpawnProcess. On shutdown or rebalance, flusher processes are never terminated.
Several new comments restate the code (lines 59, 82, 92, 241, 336)

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
'if not process: continue' can never be true since self.processes only holds started Process or Thread objects which are always truthy.
Inconsistent metric tag key: lines 185 and 195 use 'shard' while line 199 (spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) uses 'shards'.

isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always False for SpawnProcess objects created via get_context('spawn').Process(), since SpawnProcess inherits from BaseProcess, not multiprocessing.Process, causing process.kill() and process.terminate() to never be called
The docstring says 'Creates one process per shard' but the CLI default --flusher-processes=1 runs a single process for all shards in production.

In join(), once the deadline passes, the 'remaining_time <= 0: break' exits the loop before terminate() runs for the current process and all later ones, creating a gap once the isinstance guard bug is fixed.

In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.

Defaults disagree: SpanFlusher and ProcessSpansStrategyFactory default max_processes to None (one per shard), while CLI default is 1 (one process for all shards); tests exercise per-shard path, leaving multi-shard production config untested
The hasattr/isinstance anti-pattern guidance added at lines 448-458 has nothing to do with the span-flusher change and is out of scope for this PR.

On restart, hung or unhealthy flusher is never killed because isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always False for spawn-context processes (SpawnProcess), so kill() is skipped, leaving old processes unmonitored and allowing duplicate flushers

The 'shard' tag value at lines 185 and 195 is a comma-joined list of a process's shards which changes on every rebalance and has high cardinality, while line 244 tags a single int under the same key and existing buffer metrics use 'shard_i' for this concept.
Guard 'if not process: continue' in _ensure_processes_alive can never fire because self.processes only holds started Process or Thread objects which are always truthy

Docstring 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing' is wrong for default deployment where CLI default of 1 runs all shards in one process; comments at lines 178 and 235 also don't match code

The added time.sleep(0.1) commented 'Give flusher threads time to process' does nothing because line 15 already monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op, so the comment is false and the race condition remains.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

When the deadline is exceeded, break exits the loop and skips calling terminate() on the remaining flusher processes. Those processes will keep running (potentially flushing stale data) until the parent process exits. Should terminate all remaining processes before breaking.

The parent keeps one SpansBuffer per child, and every submit() loops over all of them, causing N record_stored_segments pipelines and N cluster-wide get_memory_info INFO calls against the same Redis cluster instead of one, adding unnecessary I/O on the consumer main thread.
When timeout elapses in join(), the break exits the loop without terminating remaining flusher processes, leaving background workers running during shutdown/rebalance

If --flusher-processes is set to a negative integer, SpanFlusher computes a negative num_processes and crashes while distributing shards because process_to_shards_map is empty but process_index resolves to 0, causing a KeyError

Each process gets its own SpansBuffer(shards) holding only its subset of shards, so ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)) is computed per process. This makes spans.buffer.max-flush-segments silently become a per-process budget, scaling total flush per cycle with process count and delaying backpressure.

Typo on line 199: tags={'shards': shard_tag} should be tags={'shard': shard_tag} (singular) to match the other two metrics on lines 186 and 195, causing dashboards filtering by the shard tag to silently miss the wait_produce timer
default=1 for flusher_processes forces the flusher back to a single process. Should leave unset so the existing SpanFlusher default can scale to the assigned shard count.
_create_process_for_shard is dead code: nothing in src/ or tests/ calls it

isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard may not match processes created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, causing hung children to not be killed before replacement and leaking flusher workers
Added hasattr/isinstance anti-pattern guidance in CLAUDE.md has nothing to do with span-flusher change and is scope creep

isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always False for processes created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn'), because SpawnProcess does not inherit from multiprocessing.Process. This means unhealthy processes are never killed before being restarted, and processes are never terminated during join(). Should use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or check not isinstance(process, threading.Thread) instead.

Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shards' used on wait_produce metric vs 'shard' used on flusher.produce and segment_size_bytes metrics. This will split metrics across two different tag keys in the monitoring system.
time.sleep(0.1) is patched to a no-op at the top of the test, so it doesn't actually wait for the flusher to observe the drift change, making the test timing-dependent/flaky on slower CI
--flusher-processes accepts negative integers which can make SpanFlusher.num_processes invalid and crash shard-to-process mapping/modulo at startup - should enforce minimum of 1
Inconsistent metric tag key naming: timer uses 'shards' but produce timer/segment-size metric uses 'shard', which will split metric series and complicate dashboards
Added time.sleep(0.1) does nothing because line 15 monkeypatches time.sleep to no-op for whole test; the race condition described in comment is not addressed
_create_process_for_shard (singular, line 127) is defined but never called anywhere - it's dead code that should be removed

SpansBuffer.flush_segments computes per-shard limit as ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)), making global spans.buffer.max-flush-segments option a per-process budget; total flush per cycle and backpressure threshold grow by process count factor, undocumented

test_flusher_processes_limit asserts only internal attributes (processes, max_processes, num_processes, process_to_shards_map) without producing spans or checking that segments from all 4 shards are actually flushed across several processes.

issues.claim: In SpanFlusher.join(), when the deadline expires the `break` exits the per-process loop before terminate() runs for the current and remaining flusher processes, leaving them running after join returns during shutdown/rebalance.

The isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard before process.kill() in the restart path (_ensure_processes_alive) is always False for spawn-context SpawnProcess objects, so hung or unhealthy processes are never killed before replacements start. The pre-PR code called kill() unconditionally.

In join(), terminate() sits behind the same isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check, which is always False for SpawnProcess, so flusher processes are never terminated on shutdown or rebalance.
_create_process_for_shard (lines 127-132) has no callers in src/ or tests/ and only delegates to _create_process_for_shards, so it is dead code.
Having both _create_process_for_shard and _create_process_for_shards, with near-identical names, is confusing.
In test_basic in test_consumer.py, the added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched to a no-op earlier in the test, so it does not give the flusher time to process.
test_flusher_processes_limit asserts only internal attributes and does not check that segments from all shards are flushed across multiple processes. No test covers the restart/kill path.

The CLI default for --flusher-processes is 1 (one process for all shards), while SpanFlusher and ProcessSpansStrategyFactory default max_processes to None (one per shard). This forces a single process, and tests exercise only the per-shard path.

The docstring 'Creates one process per shard' does not match the default deployment, where the CLI default of 1 runs all shards in one process. The comments at lines 178 and 235 also do not match the code.
max_processes is normalised twice, self.max_processes is kept only for the test, and _create_processes is a 2-line wrapper with one caller.

--flusher-processes is a plain int with no lower bound: 0 silently means one process per shard, and a negative value gives a negative num_processes and an empty process_to_shards_map, causing a KeyError during shard distribution.
submit() loops over one SpansBuffer per child process, calling get_memory_info() and record_stored_segments() N times against the same Redis cluster on the consumer main thread.
The spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce timer (line 199) uses tag key 'shards', while the other metrics in the same flush loop (lines 185, 195, 244) use 'shard'.

The 'shard' tag value at lines 185 and 195 is a comma-joined list of a process's shards, which changes on rebalance and has high cardinality. Line 244 tags a single int under the same key, and existing buffer metrics use 'shard_i'.
Several new comments (lines 59, 82, 92, 241, 336) restate the code.
The `if not process: continue` guard in _ensure_processes_alive can never be true, because self.processes only holds started Process or Thread objects, which are always truthy.
The hasattr/isinstance anti-pattern guidance added to CLAUDE.md (lines 448-458) is unrelated to the span-flusher change.

Each process's SpansBuffer computes ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)) over only its own shard subset, so spans.buffer.max-flush-segments becomes a per-process budget. Total flush per cycle and the backpressure threshold therefore scale with process count.
